articles.title: A Georgia woman who was trafficked at a Super 8 hotel at 15 testified that staff refused to help her escape; a federal jury awarded $164 million against the operator, including $120 million in punitive damages
articles.summary: A woman who was sexually exploited at a Georgia hotel as a teenager has won $164 million in damages from the property's former operator.
articles.body: A woman who was sexually exploited at a Georgia hotel as a teenager has won $164 million in damages from the property's former operator. A federal jury in Atlanta found against Lincoln Bancorp LLC in a case involving trafficking at a Super 8 by Wyndham in College Park.According to Atlanta Journal Constitution, the woman was 15 when the alleged exploitation began in 2020. It continued into 2021, when she was 16. During her testimony, she described how hotel employees failed to help her get away from the situation. Her lawyers argued that the company should be held responsible for what happened at the property.The jury delivered its decision in September. It awarded the woman $44 million for the harm she suffered and imposed a further $120 million in punitive damages. The total award came to $164 million.The hotel was located on Old National Highway, near Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. Lincoln Bancorp owned and operated the Super 8 property from December 2019 until December 2021.The plaintiff's legal team believes the award could be the largest verdict of its kind. The decision also comes amid several other sex trafficking cases involving hotels in Georgia.$120 million awarded as punitive damagesOf the $164 million awarded, $120 million was imposed as punitive damages. The remaining $44 million was awarded as compensation for the injuries suffered by the woman.The verdict follows an earlier case in Atlanta in which a jury awarded $40 million in damages in July 2025. That case involved the United Inn & Suites on Memorial Drive in DeKalb County.The latest decision is another major financial penalty involving allegations of trafficking at a hotel. The legal claims in such cases can involve the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorisation Act (TVPRA), which allows victims to seek damages from businesses that knowingly benefit from sex trafficking.Other Georgia hotels have faced trafficking casesThe $164 million verdict is part of a wider series of lawsuits involving hotels in Georgia. Several properties have faced claims that their owners or operators allowed trafficking to take place or benefited from it.In June 2024, Red Roof Inn settled a sex trafficking case involving two hotels in the Atlanta area. The settlement came while the case was being heard in federal court.Another case involved the Days Inn & Suites in Stockbridge. The hotel agreed to pay $5 million in September 2025 to resolve a federal lawsuit brought by two women.The women alleged that hotel employees helped their trafficker sell them at the property in 2013. They were 14 at the time.The United Inn & Suites case also continued to have legal consequences beyond the original jury verdict. In April 2026, the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the hotel would have to face two additional sex trafficking lawsuits.These cases have placed hotel operators under scrutiny over their responsibility to identify and respond to trafficking on their premises.The latest Atlanta verdict adds another substantial award to the growing number of sex trafficking cases brought against hotel businesses in Georgia.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Completely false': NCP (SP) rejects merger buzz after Supriya Sule says talks ended with Ajit Pawar's death
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) on Saturday dismissed reports of a possible merger with the Ajit Pawar-led faction as
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) on Saturday dismissed reports of a possible merger with the Ajit Pawar-led faction as "completely false", saying it had no plans to merge with any other political party.NCP (SP) spokesperson Pravin Kunte Patil alleged that the reports were being deliberately circulated to divert public attention from pressing issues such as drought, inflation, unemployment, alleged vote theft and irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations."Our official stand is that those who wish to merge should join our party," Kunte Patil said, PTI reported.His remarks came amid renewed speculation about a possible reunion between the two NCP factions: the one led by Sharad Pawar and the other headed by Maharashtra Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar.Earlier in the day, NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said discussions about a merger had ended for her following the death of her cousin, former NCP chief Ajit Pawar. She also said she had received no communication from leaders of the other faction on the matter.Speaking to reporters, Sule said merger discussions had taken place when Ajit Pawar was alive and that a date had even been decided. However, she said the discussions came to an end after his death."When my brother (then NCP chief Ajit Pawar) was alive, there were discussions about a merger. A date had also been decided. But the day my brother passed away, the merger issue came to a full stop for me and within our party," Sule said.She said her party had neither made any announcement on a merger after Ajit Pawar's death nor responded to statements from the other faction."No spokesperson from our side has spoken on this issue in the last several months," she said. Sule also said she had received no communication from the Ajit Pawar faction about a possible merger."Not a single phone call, WhatsApp message, SMS, letter or email has come to me from anyone in the Ajit Pawar faction regarding a merger. Nobody has contacted me. No one has met me regarding this," she added.Sule said her relationship with Ajit Pawar was based on affection and not political considerations, adding that she did not see the point of discussing a merger after his death."For you, this may be a discussion or gossip. For us, these are emotions. Some things are done from the heart. My relationship with my brother was that of love and affection. He is no longer here. What is the point of discussing it now?" she said.Asked whether talks could be held with Ajit Pawar's family, including his wife Sunetra Pawar, Sule said personal relationships should not be mixed with politics.Sule also rejected speculation that the NCP (SP) could join the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA)."There has been no discussion on joining the NDA. When there has been no beginning, where does the question of a full stop arise?" she said.She declined to comment on statements made by senior leaders of the Ajit Pawar faction, including Chhagan Bhujbal, Sunil Tatkare, Praful Patel and Hasan Mushrif."These are senior leaders who have worked with my father. I am much younger than them in age and experience. The values my parents taught me are that one should not speak disrespectfully about people who are older or more experienced," she said.Expressing frustration over repeated questions about a possible merger, Sule urged the media to focus on policy issues and hold political leaders accountable. She said she was "already bored with the subject"."There are several important issues facing the country and the world. There are serious policy-making issues that need to be discussed. The FCRA Bill, One Nation, One Election and several other important issues are before us. We should be discussing these issues," she said.On her meetings with senior NCP leader Praful Patel, Sule said they were related to parliamentary committee work and had no political significance."I am a member of the Finance Committee and he is also involved in committee work. We also meet in connection with the JPC on the FCRA. These are institutional meetings, not political discussions," she added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'No foreign actor involved': US transport secy blames router provider for aviation shutdown; normalcy expected by Sunday
articles.summary: The US aviation system has returned to full operations after a nationwide ground stop disrupted thousands of flights, with officials saying the disruption
articles.body: The US aviation system has returned to full operations after a nationwide ground stop disrupted thousands of flights, with officials saying the disruption was triggered by technical problems during maintenance work and not by foreign actors.Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said the work was being carried out by telecommunications contractor L3Harris as part of a long-running effort to modernise the country’s air traffic control network. A router being worked on began flooding other air traffic control systems, creating communication problems with aircraft and prompting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to halt flights as a precaution.Duffy said investigators were examining whether the incident resulted from a faulty piece of equipment or incompetence on the contractor’s part. L3Harris had not commented on the outage as of the press conference.The disruption had initially raised concerns about a possible cyberattack or foreign interference. Duffy said FBI director Kash Patel, director of national intelligence Jay Clayton and other officials joined a conference call on Friday because of concerns about whether the incident involved a cyberattack or a threat from another country. The White House Situation Room was also involved, with national security agencies brought in to examine the incident.However, officials are now confident that the disruption had a technical cause. FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said investigators had found “zero evidence of anything nefarious” and no evidence that artificial intelligence was involved.Thousands of flights affectedThe FAA ordered a four-hour ground stop while authorities investigated the problem and worked to stabilise the system. Bedford said the stoppage was intended to reduce pressure on the network while officials assessed the safety of operations.Of the roughly 20,000 flights affected, the FAA managed to recover about 8,000 during the ground stop. Around 12,000 could not be recovered, including approximately 9,000 commercial flights and 3,000 private and general aviation flights.Although the system was stable on Saturday morning, Bedford estimated that between 4,000 and 5,000 of the 41,000 flights scheduled for the day could still be cancelled. He said the worst of the disruption was over.Passengers affected by cancellations should contact their airlines directly, Bedford said. Carriers should either re-accommodate them on another flight or provide a full refund.Officials warn ageing infrastructure remains a riskDuffy said the incident had exposed the vulnerabilities of an ageing telecommunications network used by the country's air traffic control system. The replacement of copper wiring with fibre has been under way for years, but he said the existing infrastructure would remain in use until a new system is built.He defended carrying out the upgrade during the day, saying the work took place at a remote location and should not have caused such widespread disruption. At larger facilities, similar switchovers are generally carried out at night because they can have a greater impact on operations.Bedford said the system was operating as safely as it had two weeks earlier, but warned that failures would continue unless the infrastructure was replaced. Duffy renewed his appeal for Congress to approve $50 billion to build a new air traffic control system, asking how long the country could afford to wait for modernisation.The transportation secretary said the government would remain dependent on L3Harris, which operates the existing telecommunications network, until new infrastructure is in place.Bedford said the FAA would hold a transparent hearing into what caused the disruption and use the findings to determine what changes were needed.You use AI every day. articles.title: US Congress' top doctor Brian Monahan resigns amid misconduct probe; he forced staff to cut lawmakers' toenails
articles.summary: Dr Brian Monahan, the longtime physician responsible for providing medical care to members of the US Congress and Supreme Court justices, has left his
articles.body: Dr Brian Monahan, the longtime physician responsible for providing medical care to members of the US Congress and Supreme Court justices, has left his post amid a military investigation into allegations of misconduct, mismanagement and a toxic work environment at his office. Monahan, a two-star Navy rear admiral who served as the attending physician of the US Capitol since 2009, stepped down following complaints from Navy personnel assigned to his office. The allegations include excessive working hours, threats against staff who complained and demands to perform personal tasks for lawmakers, including cutting their toenails.Senate Majority Leader John Thune confirmed Monahan's departure on Thursday, saying, "My understanding is he's resigned."It is not known whether Monahan resigned voluntarily or was removed from the position. The Washington Post reported that Monahan said in a voicemail message that he was no longer serving with the Office of the Attending Physician. Punchbowl News reported that his departure followed a prolonged internal struggle involving allegations of mismanagement and workplace misconduct.Staff allegedly worked 70-80 hours a week, had to cut toenails of lawmakersNavy personnel assigned to the congressional medical office reportedly complained that they were routinely made to work between 70 and 80 hours a week. According to reports by Navy Times, staff members were also threatened with losing bonuses if they raised concerns or requested leave. The complaints included allegations that sailors were assigned duties beyond their medical responsibilities, such as clipping lawmakers' toenails and delivering medication to their private residences in the middle of the night.Some personnel reportedly had to work extended shifts when Congress remained in session late into the night and return to duty early the following morning.A former Navy hospital corpsman described working 12-hour shifts, with duty every other day, and said staff could sometimes remain at work until 4 am before returning for a regular 6 am shift.The allegations reportedly span several years, with complaints about the working environment dating back more than a decade.Pentagon watchdog flags prescription drug oversightMonahan's departure coincided with the release of a Defense Department inspector general report that identified serious shortcomings in the oversight of the congressional medical office. The report found gaps in clinical quality management and inadequate monitoring of prescription medications. Investigators discovered discrepancies in pharmacy inventories, including shortages of sleep medication compared with recorded stock levels. Other controlled substances also had inventory discrepancies.The watchdog warned that the absence of proper clinical oversight could expose patients to health and safety risks because prescribing practices were not being adequately monitored.The report made five recommendations to improve supervision and accountability at the office, including appointing an independent organisation to oversee clinical quality and establishing clearer policies and procedures.The Navy is also conducting a separate investigation into the office and the allegations involving Monahan.Who is Brian Monahan?Monahan had served as the attending physician of the US Capitol since 2009. The Office of the Attending Physician provides medical services to members of Congress, congressional staff, Supreme Court justices and visitors to the Capitol complex. Its responsibilities extend beyond routine medical treatment and include emergency medical support, prescriptions, referrals, vaccinations and planning for medical emergencies and disasters involving the Capitol.A physician certified in internal medicine, hematology and medical oncology, Monahan previously served as the personal physician to former Senate Republican leader Mitch McConnell.Neither Monahan nor the Navy had publicly provided a detailed response to the allegations at the time of the reports.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Thousands of people took to the streets of Edinburgh to protest against plans to build large-scale AI data centres across Scotland, raising concerns over
articles.body: Thousands of people took to the streets of Edinburgh to protest against plans to build large-scale AI data centres across Scotland, raising concerns over their environmental impact, electricity consumption and potential increase in energy bills.Demonstrators gathered at the top of the Royal Mile before marching towards the Scottish Parliament, carrying placards with slogans such as "AI data centres threaten humanity", "AI data centres: costing the Earth" and "People before data centres".More than 80 organisations and groups, including climate campaigners, trade unions, community groups and anti-poverty charities, took part in the demonstration, according to The Herald.The protest comes amid growing opposition to large-scale data centre projects across Europe, with campaigners demanding greater public consultation before such developments are approved.According to BBC, some protesters were particularly concerned about proposed projects in communities including Cockenzie in East Lothian, Larbert in Falkirk and Chapelcross in Dumfries and Galloway.Kim Cairns, a campaigner with Say No To Chapelcross AI Data Centre, told BBC Scotland News that residents were worried about construction-related disruption, road closures, noise and the long-term impact of the facility."It's not going to enrich anybody's lives. For Chapelcross it's the sheer size of it, the amount of electricity it's going to need," she said, describing the proposed development as a "monstrosity on the environment".The scale of the proposed projects has become a major concern. Scotland's largest existing data centre, operated by DataVita in Airdrie, has a capacity of around 12 megawatts. However, the proposed Chapelcross facility could have a capacity of 1,000 megawatts, potentially making it one of the largest data centres in the world.Campaigners have also warned that the projects could put additional pressure on Scotland's electricity supply and undermine its climate targets.Friends of the Earth Scotland senior campaigner Kim Pratt said the developments could benefit major technology companies while leaving local communities to bear the environmental and financial costs.Meanwhile, the Scottish government said it would publish new planning guidance on data centres before the end of the year. It also said planning authorities would have to notify ministers about new applications, while projects exceeding 50 megawatts would require an Environmental Impact Assessment.The Scottish Greens and campaign groups have called for a moratorium on large data centres until their wider impact is assessed.You use AI every day. articles.summary: At least 24 terrorists and four Pakistani soldiers, including an army officer, were killed in separate encounters between security forces and militants in
articles.body: At least 24 terrorists and four Pakistani soldiers, including an army officer, were killed in separate encounters between security forces and militants in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces, the Pakistan Army said on Saturday, PTI reported.The army said security forces had carried out multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan since Friday, targeting militant hideouts in the areas of Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki.During an operation in Kolpur on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday, troops killed eight terrorists, including a suicide bomber, and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition, the military said.The army said the militants used armed quadcopters to target military vehicles on patrol. The attack killed Major Omer Minhas Nasir and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan.The Pakistani government last year designated terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as 'Fitna al Hindustan'. Islamabad has alleged that these outfits carry out terrorist activities at India's behest, but has not provided evidence to support the claim.In June, India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations over the use of the term, calling it "officially sponsored misinformation and disinformation dressed in religious terminology."Separately, security forces conducted operations against militant hideouts in Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas of North Waziristan district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the military's media wing, 16 militants were killed in the engagements. Twelve were killed in an operation in Ali Khel, while two each were killed in Mir Ali and Datta Khel.Two soldiers, Havildar Asmat Ali and Naik Aftab Ali, were killed during the operations. The ISPR said both soldiers fought bravely and laid down their lives in the line of duty. It added that the operations had dealt a major blow to the militant network.Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain militants, who, according to the military, were involved in several terrorist activities, including the killing of civilians.Pakistan's federal government uses the term 'Fitna al-Khawarij' for militants belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).You use AI every day. articles.body: A Canadian forestry company has donated more than 1,800 hectares of forest, wetlands and freshwater shoreline in central Newfoundland and Labrador to support a major conservation initiative around Gander Lake. The donation from Domtar will allow the Nature Conservancy of Canada (NCC) to protect four parcels of land along the Southwest Gander River and Gander Lake, near Glenwood and Appleton. The project aims to improve wildlife movement across connected natural habitats while safeguarding important ecosystems in a region where relatively little land is formally protected.Domtar's 1,800-hectare donation strengthens conservation around Gander LakeThe Nature Conservancy of Canada announced the initiative on October 1, 2025, describing it as the largest land donation it had received during its 54 years of conservation work in Atlantic Canada. According to the organisation's announcement, the donation covers more than 1,800 hectares, equivalent to approximately 4,400 acres, of boreal forest, freshwater shoreline and wetlands.The land is spread across 4 large parcels situated along the Southwest Gander River and Gander Lake. These properties are close to the communities of Glenwood and Appleton, placing the conservation initiative within an important landscape of central Newfoundland.Domtar's contribution will enable NCC to conserve the land rather than leave its long-term protection dependent on future decisions about its use. The company said the initiative reflected its commitment to environmental stewardship and preserving Canada's natural heritage.Why is connected wildlife habitat important in central NewfoundlandThe donation has particular significance because of the limited amount of protected land in the surrounding region. The Nature Conservancy of Canada and Domtar reported that less than 3% of the Central Newfoundland ecoregion currently falls under conservation status.This means large areas of natural habitat remain outside established protected areas, making connections between conservation sites particularly valuable.According to NCC, the donated properties could help wildlife move more easily between existing and potential conservation lands. The initiative also has the potential to connect two proposed protected areas, the province's Rodney Pond Wilderness Reserve and Charlie's Place, a conservation area proposed by Qalipu First Nation.As reported by ToDoCanada, the 4 parcels form part of a broader conservation effort intended to improve habitat connectivity while protecting important natural landscapes in central Newfoundland.Wildlife and plant species could benefit from the protected landThe donated properties contain a mixture of forests, wetlands, rivers and streams that support a range of wildlife and plant species. Much of the area is covered by boreal forest, including black spruce, balsam fir, tamarack, white birch, white spruce and trembling aspen.The surrounding waterways also contribute to the region's ecological importance. The Gander River system is one of Newfoundland's most significant watersheds for Atlantic salmon, while freshwater habitats support Arctic char and brook trout. These fish species depend on healthy aquatic environments, making the protection of surrounding forests and wetlands relevant to the wider ecosystem.The land is also within the range of the Middle Ridge caribou herd and close to the Mount Peyton caribou herd. Protecting connected landscapes can help maintain the natural habitats these animals use.Several species identified under Canada's Species at Risk Act are present in the area. NCC lists the Newfoundland pine marten and red crossbill as threatened species, while rusty blackbird and blue felt lichen are classified as being of special concern.To Do Canada also identifies large purple fringed orchids and three-way sedge among the species associated with the landscape, highlighting the importance of conserving habitats beyond forests alone.Government support will help fund long-term conservationDomtar's donation forms part of a wider partnership involving the Nature Conservancy of Canada and the Government of Canada. The federal government is supporting the project through its Natural Heritage Conservation Program, which is part of Canada's Nature Fund.The conservation organisation is encouraging local residents, businesses and foundations to contribute towards securing the properties and supporting their long-term management.The funding will also help provide for the ongoing care and management of the land, ensuring that the ecological benefits of the project can continue over time.How will the conservation project affect existing land activitiesProtecting the land does not mean eliminating all recreational activities from the area. According to the NCC, legal hunting and angling will continue once the conservation process is completed.The organisations have also outlined measures to help guide recreational use. Signs will be installed to remind all-terrain vehicle users to remain on existing trails, helping limit unnecessary disturbance to surrounding natural areas.This approach allows conservation efforts to coexist with established outdoor activities while keeping the protection of wildlife habitats central to the project.The area surrounding Gander Lake is also important for recreational fishing, particularly because of the Gander River system's significance for Atlantic salmon.Domtar has previously supported large-scale conservation in CanadaThe Newfoundland donation is not Domtar's first major contribution to conservation efforts. The company transferred stewardship of approximately 145,000 hectares of boreal forest in Ontario to the Nature Conservancy of Canada in 2022.According to NCC, the Ontario agreement formed part of the largest private land conservation agreement in Canadian history. The property near Hearst is being preserved and managed for research and long-term conservation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Is East Potomac Park closing on November 15 for 15 months? Hundreds of trees were felled until judge Ana Reyes whom Trump called 'crazed lunatic' stepped in
articles.summary: The Donald Trump administration has run into a legal tiff after it announced that it would close the East Potomac Park and the historic public golf course
articles.body: The Donald Trump administration has run into a legal tiff after it announced that it would close the East Potomac Park and the historic public golf course from November 15. While the closure is said to be for renovation and redevelopment, preservation groups and golfers sought an emergency court order to prevent the shutdown, arguing that the administration is using safety concerns as a pretext to advance Trump's plan to transform the historic public facility into a championship-level golf course. The renovation would take at least 15 months.US District Judge Ana C. Reyes heard more than five hours of arguments on Friday, November 13, but did not immediately issue a ruling on the request. She was expected to decide the matter on Saturday, a day before the planned closure.So as of now, the park will be closed today at 9 pm but the court verdict can change things.During the hearing, Reyes repeatedly questioned the administration's justification for shutting down the entire area, particularly its claims about deteriorating infrastructure and the need to address safety hazards. The judge asked why the government could not simply fence off sections considered dangerous instead of closing the entire park. She also questioned the lack of a clear funding arrangement or timeline for repairing the deteriorating seawall. The administration has argued that the closure is necessary because of safety concerns and the departure of National Links Trust, the nonprofit organization that has operated the golf course. However, the judge questioned whether the departure of the operator justified shutting down the surrounding public parkland.Why does Trump want to redevelop East Potomac Park?Trump has proposed transforming the existing East Potomac Golf Links into a championship-level golf facility capable of hosting major tournaments. The proposed redesign is associated with golf architect Tom Fazio. The plan would replace the existing public golf facilities with a new championship-style course. The administration has said the proposal is still subject to environmental and historic-preservation reviews and public consultation.The National Park Service's planned closure covers the area south of Buckeye Drive, including the golf course, Ohio Drive, waterfront promenade, fishing areas and other recreational facilities.The Justice Department has said the closure is separate from the proposed redevelopment. However, government lawyers acknowledged in court that Trump had directed the closure.This is a historic park: Preservation groups challenge administration in courtThe DC Preservation League and two regular golfers filed a lawsuit in February challenging the administration's plans for East Potomac Golf Links. The plaintiffs argued that the proposed redevelopment could cause irreversible damage to the historic park and restrict public access. They have also accused the administration of moving ahead without completing the environmental and historic-preservation reviews required for major changes to the site.The legal dispute intensified in October after hundreds of trees were removed from the golf course.On October 26, Reyes issued a preliminary injunction prohibiting the administration from cutting down or damaging additional trees without court approval. The order also required the government to provide advance written notice before closing the course or making other irreversible changes.The Trump administration appealed the injunction, but Reyes refused to suspend it on November 9.The preservation groups then filed an emergency request seeking to prevent the November 15 closure while the broader lawsuit continues.Judge launches inquiry into whether Trump administration misled courtDuring an earlier hearing in October, officials from the Interior Department and National Park Service appeared unaware of Trump's publicly announced November 15 closure plan when questioned by the judge. The conflicting accounts prompted Reyes to pursue an inquiry into whether administration officials and government lawyers misled the court about the redevelopment plans and the removal of hundreds of trees.On Saturday, November 14, Reyes said the inquiry would proceed despite the Justice Department's objections. She indicated that she was prepared to oversee the investigation herself.The judge had identified former US attorney Jessie K. Liu as a possible special master to examine whether government officials and lawyers violated their ethical obligations. However, she did not decide on Friday whether to appoint Liu, after the Justice Department challenged the proposed appointment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Wisconsin daughter accused her brother of mishandling their mother's two family trusts and sought his removal as trustee; a November 10 appeals court upheld a contempt finding for his failure to provide documents
articles.summary: A dispute over the management of two family trusts in Wisconsin has resulted in an appeals court upholding a contempt finding against a brother who failed
articles.body: A dispute over the management of two family trusts in Wisconsin has resulted in an appeals court upholding a contempt finding against a brother who failed to provide requested financial documents to his sister. The case centred on whether his attempt to disqualify his sister's lawyer justified delaying his discovery responses.In a November 10, 2026, decision in Anne M Bartnik v. Todd A Mackoway, available in Justia, the Wisconsin Court of Appeals affirmed a Marathon County Circuit Court order finding Todd A Mackoway in remedial contempt. The court concluded that he had other legal options to address the discovery deadline but failed to use them.Sister sought brother's removal as trusteeThe dispute began on February 17, 2025, when Anne M Bartnik filed a verified petition seeking to remove her brother as successor general trustee of their mother Shirley Mackoway's two trusts. Bartnik alleged that Mackoway had breached his fiduciary duties by failing to administer the trusts effectively, prudently, impartially and in good faith. She also argued that his alleged hostility towards her made him unsuitable to continue as trustee.She asked the court to require him to provide complete trust accounting records, including information about property, liabilities, receipts and disbursements. Her petition also sought inventories, supporting documents and judicial review of his conduct as their mother's healthcare and financial agent. Mackoway filed a motion to dismiss the claims concerning his conduct as their mother's agent in March 2025. The court initially stayed discovery but denied his motion on July 24. He filed his response to the petition the following month.Dispute over discovery and lawyer's disqualificationOn September 24, 2025, Bartnik served Mackoway with written discovery requests, including interrogatories and document production requests. He was required to respond within 30 days. On October 22, Mackoway's lawyer contacted Bartnik's attorney, Mary Sue Anderson, claiming that Mackoway had previously consulted her about the same matter as a prospective client. He argued that the consultation required Anderson to withdraw from representing his sister.Mackoway filed a motion seeking Anderson's disqualification and informed Bartnik's legal team that he would not attend a scheduled deposition or provide written discovery responses until the issue was resolved. Bartnik filed motions for remedial contempt and to compel discovery on October 27, arguing that her brother had neither met his obligations nor sought an extension or protective order.The circuit court rejected the disqualification motion on January 5, 2026. Mackoway sent his discovery responses on January 23, but the production remained incomplete. Bartnik's attorney, Mary Sue Anderson, said she had received no substantive documents in response to requests one through seven, some documents for request eight, and nothing for requests nine through 14.Circuit court found contempt over missed deadlineAt a February 4, 2026, hearing, the circuit court distinguished between Mackoway's failure to attend his deposition and his failure to provide written discovery responses. It accepted that his decision not to attend the deposition was made in good faith while the disqualification motion remained pending. However, it found that his written responses had been due on October 24, 2025, and that the pending motion did not automatically suspend that obligation.The court noted that Mackoway had not sought an extension or stay before the deadline. It ordered him to provide complete responses by February 11, 2026, and pay Bartnik's reasonable attorney fees relating to the contempt motion.Appeals court upheld contempt findingMackoway appealed, arguing that his failure to respond was not intentional because he believed discovery should pause until the court decided the disqualification issue. The appeals court disagreed, explaining that an intentional refusal to produce requested records can constitute contempt under Wisconsin law. Mackoway could have formally objected to the requests, sought a protective order or asked the court to delay the response deadline.Instead, he allowed the deadline to pass without obtaining court approval. The appeals court also noted that he failed to provide complete responses immediately after the disqualification motion was denied. It rejected his argument that the circuit court had treated his deposition absence and written discovery failure inconsistently. The deposition raised separate concerns about potentially confidential information shared during the alleged consultation, while the written requests related generally to the claims in Bartnik's petition.The Wisconsin Court of Appeals affirmed the contempt order on November 10, 2026. The ruling addresses the discovery dispute, not the underlying allegations of trustee misconduct or whether Mackoway should ultimately be removed.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'The Last of Us' series brought more than $141 million in production spending to Alberta; a study found its filming supported 1,490 full-time jobs
articles.summary: The success of HBO's The Last of Us extended beyond its television audience, bringing a major production operation to Alberta and generating millions of
articles.body: The success of HBO's The Last of Us extended beyond its television audience, bringing a major production operation to Alberta and generating millions of dollars in local economic activity. Filmed across towns, cities and some of the province's best-known landscapes, the first season created work for the Canadian cast and crew while bringing business to hotels, construction suppliers and catering companies. An economic assessment by Oxford Economics, released in November 2023, put the production spending at more than $141 million. The filming also supported 1,490 jobs and generated over C$182 million in contributions to Alberta's gross domestic product.How HBO's The Last of Us became Canada's largest television productionThe first season of The Last of Us, adapted from the popular video game franchise, was filmed across several parts of Alberta. Its production brought together locations ranging from urban settings to smaller communities and landscapes that could stand in for a post-apocalyptic version of North America.The scale of the operation made it particularly significant for Canada's television industry. According to figures released by the Motion Picture Association – Canada (MPA Canada) on November 27, 2023, the HBO series was the largest television series ever filmed in the country at that time, measured by its production scale and economic impact.The assessment, prepared by Oxford Economics, examined how money spent during filming moved through Alberta's economy. Rather than limiting the calculation to the production company's direct expenses, it considered spending on workers and the businesses supplying goods and services.How The Last of Us distributed $141 million among workers and local businessesOf the more than $141 million spent in Alberta, approximately $71 million went towards wages and salaries for local cast members, crew and other production personnel. The remaining $70 million was directed towards businesses operating across the province.Film productions depend on materials for constructing sets, transport, accommodation, food services and other everyday requirements. Local construction companies, hotels, catering providers and suppliers of production equipment were among the businesses that could benefit from the spending associated with the series.More than 1,000 Alberta businesses were involved in supplying goods and services to the production. This meant the financial activity was not confined to the studios or the immediate filming locations. Companies in different parts of the province became part of the operation, including businesses that would not normally be associated with television production.The Last of Us supported 1,490 jobs and earned Canadian crew Emmy recognitionThe Oxford Economics assessment calculated that The Last of Us supported a total of 1,490 jobs in Alberta. The figure reflected employment generated through the production's wider economic activity, rather than simply counting the principal actors and people directly employed on set.Production work can involve a sizeable network of occupations. Alongside camera operators, designers, technicians and other film professionals, large projects require people working in construction, hospitality, transport, food services and supply companies.The series also provided opportunities for Canadian creative professionals to contribute to an internationally distributed television production. Several members of the Canadian team received recognition through the show's 24 Emmy nominations, which included categories covering production design, hairstyling, makeup, costumes and sound mixing.The production generated $182 million for Alberta’s economyThe production's financial contribution was not limited to the money paid out during filming. The economic assessment estimated that its activities generated more than C$182 million in Alberta's gross domestic product.GDP measures the value added through economic activity, making it different from the amount a production spends directly. The figure reflects the wider contribution associated with the project, including the activity generated among businesses and workers connected to the production.The impact also extended to smaller communities where production teams worked and spent money. For businesses in these locations, a television production can bring temporary demand for accommodation, meals, equipment and other services that might otherwise come from a different source.More than 180 filming locations spread the production across AlbertaAlberta's geography played an important part in the production. Filming took place in communities including Canmore, Fort Macleod and Waterton, alongside other locations spread across the province.The production involved more than 180 filming locations distributed across a stretch of terrain exceeding 1,000 kilometres, according to Alberta Film Commissioner Mark Ham. Coordinating work across such a large area required support from regional film commissions, which helped the production navigate local locations and logistical arrangements.The settings also gave viewers a glimpse of Alberta's varied landscapes. The province offered a combination of towns, larger urban areas, open prairies, forests and Rocky Mountain scenery, allowing the production to create different environments as the story moved west.There was a possible longer-term benefit for the communities featured on screen, too. Television audiences sometimes seek out places they recognise from popular productions, creating opportunities for local tourism businesses. Visitors travelling to filming locations can generate spending at restaurants, hotels and other attractions, although the 2023 assessment did not establish a separate tourism revenue figure for the series.Government incentives helped attract the productionAlberta's film and television industry had been developing its position as a destination for international productions, supported by financial incentives, industry training and access to local technical workers. The province's Film and Television Tax Credit was among the measures associated with attracting The Last of Us. The programme was designed to encourage production companies to spend money in Alberta and make use of its workforce and filming infrastructure.Alberta's then Jobs, Economy and Trade Minister Matt Jones said, “The Last of Us, the largest series ever filmed in Canada, has left an indelible mark on Alberta’s economic landscape.” “Supported by Alberta’s Film and Television Tax Credit, this monumental production not only showcased the breathtaking facets of our province but also emphasized why Alberta, with over 180 diverse filming locations, is a world-class destination for large-scale film and television productions.”You use AI every day. Instead of directly providing answers, AI uses adaptive Socratic questioning and feedback to help students arrive at solutions independently.She said the approach discourages “cognitive offloading” by students and promotes deeper engagement with subject matter. Discussions at the forum also highlighted findings from Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) research that the educational benefits of AI depend largely on how the technology is used. articles.body: Lucknow: A march by hundreds of advocates towards Vidhan Bhavan on Saturday to press for the implementation of an Advocates’ Protection Act threw traffic out of gear across several parts of the city, leaving hundreds of vehicles stranded for nearly two hours.Traffic movement was severely affected in Hazratganj, Kaiserbagh, Parivartan Chowk and adjoining areas as police barricaded several major roads leading to the Assembly complex.The march began around noon from the district court premises in Kaiserbagh, with the advocates proceeding through Parivartan Chowk, KD Singh Babu Stadium, Halwasiya and Hazratganj towards Vidhan Bhavan.The Burlington-Hazratganj stretch was among the worst affected, with traffic piling up on the road connecting Burlington Crossing, Vidhan Bhavan, Hazratganj Crossing and Shriram Tower. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Referring to the revamped Agnipath scheme, Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, during the passing-out parade of the largest batch of over
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Referring to the revamped Agnipath scheme, Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, during the passing-out parade of the largest batch of over 3,300 trainees, including 2,756 Agniveers, of Indian Navy and Naviks of Indian Coast Guard at INS Chilka in Odisha on Friday, said they now have an “additional opportunity” to become a regular sailor.With the revamped Agnipath scheme offering the remaining 75% of Agniveers (25% are already absorbed in the forces as regulars) an opportunity to be regular soldiers, the Navy chief informed the trainees that they now possess a concrete pathway to secure a long-term, rewarding career as regular sailors. This marks a major departure from the original framework, establishing this graduating group as the first to directly benefit from the revised Agnipath rules.“With 3,358 trainees passing out in a single batch, this is the largest single batch ever at (INS) Chilka. Among them are 142 women Agniveers, who today become role models for millions. Somewhere in a small town or village, a young girl watching them will say, ‘I also wish to do this’,” the Admiral said.“Remember, you are among a select few who have earned the privilege of wearing this uniform. Of the lakhs of young aspirants that applied, only about 1.5% made it through. You are among them. You have earned your place through a very competitive selection process. And you are joining the Navy at a particularly opportune time,” the Navy chief said.“The Navy can offer you the opportunity, but you must earn it through your performance, conduct, behaviour, commitment and competitiveness. So, work hard from day one, make the most of every facility and opportunity you get, and strive to be among the best,” he said.Talking about the changing warfare, Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan said, “When I joined the Navy in 1987, the world was a very different place. Today, the battle space has changed tremendously. Satellites, drones, AI, quantum technologies and autonomous systems are changing how we fight at sea. Warfare is indeed transformed very rapidly. Of the lakhs of young aspirants that applied, only about 1.5% made it through. You are among them. You have earned your place through a very competitive selection process. And you are joining the Navy at a particularly opportune time.”In his address, the reviewing officer complimented the trainees for their immaculate turnout and very high standards of drill.He exhorted them to uphold the highest standards of discipline, integrity and professionalism, adapt to the evolving demands of maritime operations and discharge their duties with pride and an unwavering commitment to the nation.

articles.title: Preparations for self-enumeration second phase begin in Bahraich
articles.summary: Bahraich gears up for Census phase 2 as 15-day self-enumeration drive starts Monday; residents can submit family details online, with support helplines.
articles.body: Bahraich: Preparations for the second phase of the Census in Bahraich district have been completed, with a 15-day self-enumeration campaign scheduled to begin on Monday. Under the initiative, residents will be able to enter their family details online from the comfort of their homes. Officials and employees involved in the census process have undergone 15 days of training to ensure the smooth implementation of the campaign.During a programme organised at the Udyan Auditorium, DM Rajesh Kumar Pandey appealed to the public to actively participate in the campaign. He said people’s cooperation would make the census process easier and help enumerators complete their work within the stipulated time.Representatives of public bodies, voluntary organisations, government offices, employees of the Economics and Statistics Department and individuals associated with Panchayati Raj institutions would also participate in the exercise.Residents have been advised to keep the ID generated after completing their self-enumeration safely. When enumerators visit their homes, they will need to provide this ID to facilitate verification and completion of the census process. This will help ensure that the exercise is completed efficiently and within the scheduled timeframe.Officials said the self-enumeration process was demonstrated during the training programme and no major network-related difficulties were encountered. In case of any technical or administrative problems, immediate assistance will be available through the control room established at the National Informatics Centre (NIC). A state-level team and senior officials will also remain available to provide support whenever required.To create awareness among residents, particularly in rural areas, tutorial materials have been prepared and awareness posters are being displayed in villages. articles.summary: Lucknow Police deploy three-tier security with drones, CCTV, plainclothes staff and water teams at Chhath Puja ghats; traffic measures across 157 sites.
articles.body: Lucknow: Ahead of Chhath Puja on Nov 15 and 16, Lucknow Police rolled out a three-tier security plan at major ghats, with drones, CCTV cameras and plainclothes personnel deployed to ensure devotees’ safety.Enhanced security arrangements were made at Laxman Mela Ground, Kudiya Ghat, Jhulelal Ghat and G-20 Ghat, where large crowds are expected for the evening and morning rituals. Barricading has also been put up at vulnerable points.CCTV cameras and drones will monitor crowd movement and help police detect congestion or security threats. Personnel will be deployed at multiple levels to regulate entry and exit and respond to emergencies.Male and female officers in plain clothes will keep watch on suspicious activity and ensure the safety of women and children. SDRF and water police teams will remain stationed at sensitive locations to handle any water-related emergencies.Chhath Puja celebrations will be organised at a total of 157 locations across the Lucknow Police Commissionerate area. Of these, 47 venues fall under the East Zone, 17 under the West Zone, eight under the North Zone, 63 under the South Zone and 22 under the Central Zone.Joint commissioner of police (law and order) Babloo Kumar said all major ghats had been brought under a comprehensive security cover, with surveillance and emergency-response teams deployed. “Traffic police have also been directed to ensure smooth vehicular movement and prevent congestion around the ghats,” said Kumar.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Spate of ragging cases forces NMC to direct strict action
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A spate of disturbing ragging complaints by first-year MBBS students - ranging from being forced to imitate sexual acts, change clothes in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A spate of disturbing ragging complaints by first-year MBBS students - ranging from being forced to imitate sexual acts, change clothes in front of others to late-night humiliation and social boycotts - has prompted National Medical Commission (NMC) to issue 18 notices or communications to 15 medical colleges between Oct 16 and Nov 11.The complaints, received by NMC's anti-ragging cell, concern 14 colleges in Rajasthan and one in Karnataka. They allege physical and verbal abuse, sexual humiliation, coercive activities, restrictions on juniors' movement, and threats of academic retaliation.The action comes amid a separate ragging case at Govt Medical College, Jalaun, UP, where videos of alleged harassment of junior students surfaced online in Oct.The college initially suspended seven senior students for a week. Following a wider inquiry, 10 more were found involved, taking the total to 17 students, who were subsequently suspended for three months and fined Rs 25,000 each.In most cases, NMC sought detailed action taken reports within 24 hours, directing colleges to identify those involved, preserve footage from CCTV cameras and digital evidence, conduct impartial inquiries and protect complainants from intimidation.It has advised colleges to take the strictest action against students found guilty, including suspension or cancellation of their medical registration, an NMC official told TOI. Citing Gujarat as an example, he said some students' registrations had been suspended there.He stressed that enforcement largely rested with state authorities and medical councils, adding lenient approach has often allowed offenders to escape action. "NMC will support the harshest action, provided due process is followed," the official said.Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson United Doctors Front said, "Young students enter medical colleges to build their future, not to face intimidation and exploitation. State govts must act immediately, order independent probes and hold college authorities accountable. No institution can be allowed to shield abuse in the name of tradition."Some complaints describe particularly disturbing incidents. In Rajasthan's Banswara Govt Medical College, first-year students were allegedly forced to perform degrading postures, imitate sexual acts, dance to 'item' songs and change clothes in front of others. At Churu, complaints included forced haircuts, removal of clothing and sexual humiliation.Other complaints cited coercive instructions in a "Personality Development Program" document at Sardar Patel Medical College, Bikaner, and alleged emotional and verbal abuse, with possible faculty involvement, at Karnataka's Ballari Medical College.NMC has directed the colleges to conduct confidential student interviews, provide counselling and prevent retaliation against complainants. It has also sought details of the functioning of their anti-ragging committees and squads.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: An Indiana father challenged child-support payments after his two daughters moved in with him and stopped visiting their mother; on November 12, appeals judges awarded him $15,275 and reinstated her support duty
articles.summary: When children move from one parent's home to the other's, existing child-support arrangements may need to be revised to reflect who is actually providing
articles.body: When children move from one parent's home to the other's, existing child-support arrangements may need to be revised to reflect who is actually providing their care. An Indiana family dispute raised this issue after two daughters moved in with their father at different times and stopped visiting their mother, leading to disagreements over financial contributions, parenting-time credits and continuing support obligations.In a November 12, 2026, decision in Joseph E Foster v. Brigitte M Foster, available on Justia, the Indiana Court of Appeals partly reversed a lower court's child-support calculations and directed it to enter a judgment of $15,275.16 in favour of the father. The appeals judges also reinstated the mother's child-support responsibility, clarifying that a daughter's refusal to maintain contact with her mother did not automatically end the mother's obligation to provide financial support.Daughters moved into father's homeJoseph Foster and Brigitte Foster divorced in 2016 and initially shared joint physical and legal custody of their daughters, Alyson and Lauren. In November 2022, the mother received sole legal custody. The family arrangements changed on January 23, 2024, when Alyson moved into her father's home and stopped visiting her mother. The parents agreed that child support should be recalculated from that date.Alyson began attending college in August 2024 and was subsequently treated as emancipated for support purposes. On August 12, 2025, Lauren also moved into her father's home and stopped visiting her mother. The father then sought modifications to custody and child support. The parents eventually presented their competing calculations to the trial court in March 2026.Parents disagreed over expenses and overnight visitsThe father maintained that he had covered Alyson's living expenses until her emancipation and was responsible for Lauren's expenses after she moved in with him. The mother argued that she had continued contributing towards the children's needs, including Lauren's vehicle, mobile phone, medical expenses and college-credit courses. She also referred to school lunches, testing fees and other expenses she had previously paid.Another disagreement concerned parenting-time credits. The mother sought credit for 182 overnight visits with Lauren, arguing that the daughter's decision to stop visiting was not her responsibility. The father disputed this claim, pointing out that Lauren had not spent any nights at her mother's home after moving in with him. Both parents agreed that the father's weekly income was $9,038 and the mother's was $1,471.48.Lower court found father had overpaidThe Lake Circuit Court divided the support calculations into three periods. It calculated that the father owed the mother $14,442 between January 23 and August 15, 2024, and another $29,640 between August 15, 2024, and August 12, 2025. For the period after Lauren moved in with her father, the court calculated an additional $12,123, while allowing the mother credit for 182 overnight visits.The court determined that the father's total support obligation was $56,205 and that he had paid $60,568. It therefore found that he had overpaid by $4,363. The court also concluded that Lauren had repudiated her relationship with her mother without just cause and ended the mother's future child-support obligation.Appeals court rejects parenting-time creditThe Indiana Court of Appeals agreed with the calculations for the first two periods but found that the lower court had made an error when calculating support after Lauren moved. The appeals judges noted that all three family members had acknowledged that Lauren had not spent any overnight visits with her mother after moving out.Under Indiana Child Support Guideline 6, parenting-time credits must reflect actual overnight stays. The mother could not receive credit for 182 visits that had never occurred. The court recalculated her weekly support obligation for the relevant 32-week period at $71.88, resulting in an additional $2,300.16 in the father's favour.Mother's support obligation reinstatedThe appeals court also disagreed with the decision to end the mother's child-support responsibility because Lauren had rejected their relationship. It explained that a child's repudiation of a parent may, in certain circumstances, affect that parent's responsibility for college expenses. However, this does not automatically eliminate the separate obligation to provide child support. Relying on earlier Indiana decisions, including Bales v. Bales and Lovold v. Ellis, the court clarified that a child's estrangement cannot by itself serve as a defence against an existing child-support obligation.The appeals court ultimately calculated the father's overpayment at $15,275.16, based on a payment history showing that he had paid $57,057. It affirmed part of the lower court's order, reversed the disputed portions and sent the case back for further proceedings to determine the mother's remaining support obligation.You use AI every day.
